text: Always use parameterized queries or an ORM (such as SQLAlchemy) instead of building SQL strings with concatenation or f-strings. Never trust user input directly inside a query.
Store credentials in environment variables or a secrets manager (such as AWS Secrets Manager or HashiCorp Vault). Never commit API keys or passwords into source control.
Avoid writing untrusted data into innerHTML. Use textContent, or sanitize input with a library such as DOMPurify before rendering it as HTML.
Use modern hashing algorithms such as SHA-256 or bcrypt/argon2 for passwords. MD5 and SHA1 are broken and should never be used for security purposes.
Avoid eval() and exec() on any input that could be influenced by a user. Use safer alternatives like ast.literal_eval for parsing simple data.
Never unpickle data from an untrusted source. Prefer safe serialization formats like JSON for data exchange.
Never compare plaintext passwords. Hash passwords with bcrypt or argon2 and compare hashes using constant-time comparison functions.
Disable debug mode in any production deployment. Debug pages can expose stack traces, environment variables, and internal file paths to attackers.
